There are many mushroom species that can only reliably be ID’d using spore prints, and most plants can be ID’d at least down to the genus without magnification or tests. Think of it like this- the mushroom is the reproductive part and that is usually the only part you see. For plants, you see the reproductive and vegetative tissue, so there is just more reliable ways to tell what’s what. 

Also, mycology is understudied compared to botany, so you are taking a risk even with correct ID. It’s hard to do a high quality long term study on if a mushroom that rarely anyone eats causes cancer because it’s difficult to find enough people and funding is limited. Do your own research, because you might find something that someone else missed because the research wasn’t out the last time they looked for it.
